subsystems.name: Individual robot unit
subsystems.role: the basic agent that moves and acts in the environment.

subsystems.name: Sensing and perception
subsystems.role: lets each robot detect its surroundings and nearby swarm-mates.

subsystems.name: Local communication
subsystems.role: shares state and intent with robots within range.

subsystems.name: Power and energy management
subsystems.role: keeps robots running between charges or refuels.

subsystems.name: Swarm control software
subsystems.role: produces collective behaviour from simple local rules.

subsystems.name: Deployment and support infrastructure
subsystems.role: gets robots to the site and keeps them operating.

buildSteps.title: Define the mission
buildSteps.detail: Choose the environment (warehouse floor, field, water surface) and the collective goal, such as area coverage or object collection.

buildSteps.title: Design the individual robot
buildSteps.detail: Specify size, sensors, actuators, radio and battery so that one robot can perform its local task reliably.

buildSteps.title: Prototype a single unit
buildSteps.detail: Build and test one robot for mobility, sensing range and communication distance.

buildSteps.title: Develop swarm algorithms in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Use physics simulators to test coordination rules with hundreds of virtual robots before touching hardware.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a small swarm
buildSteps.detail: Manufacture or hand-build tens of identical robots, keeping unit cost low and behaviour consistent.

buildSteps.title: Run controlled experiments
buildSteps.detail: Release the swarm in an indoor arena or fenced outdoor testbed to observe emergent patterns and measure performance.

buildSteps.title: Iterate hardware and software
buildSteps.detail: Improve fault tolerance, energy use and scalability based on test failures and bottlenecks.

buildSteps.title: Scale production
buildSteps.detail: Move to batch manufacturing with reliable components and automated calibration.

buildSteps.title: Pilot in a real application
buildSteps.detail: Deploy in a structured setting such as a warehouse, farm or inspection site, with human supervision.

prerequisites.why: robots must share local state without a central hub; scaling to thousands of nodes is still challenging.
cheap, small components make it practical to build many identical robots.
long missions need energy storage that fits on a small robot.
ant-colony and flocking rules work in simulation and small tests, but robust scaling in the real world is not yet proven.
a swarm must keep working when individual robots fail; automatic recovery is still a research problem.

pathway.milestone: research testbeds with tens to hundreds of simple robots in labs and arenas
pathway.unlocks: understanding of how local rules produce collective behaviour.

pathway.milestone: pilot deployments in structured environments such as warehouses and farms
pathway.unlocks: commercial validation for specific, bounded tasks.

pathway.milestone: large-scale swarms for environmental cleanup or disaster response
pathway.unlocks: the ability to tackle problems too large or dangerous for individual robots.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous, self-organising swarms in unstructured environments
pathway.unlocks: ubiquitous use in logistics, agriculture and construction with minimal human oversight.
